questions.question: If it takes 1 hour for 60 people to play an Opera, how many hours will it take 600 people to play the same opera?
questions.a6_answer: 60 people play it in 1 hour. 600 people will take 1 / 60 = 1/60 = 16/30 = 0.5333 hours.

questions.question: Is a pound of feathers or a British pound heavier?
questions.a6_answer: A pound of feathers is heavier than the physical coin or banknote. A currency amount is money, not a unit of weight. Monetary value does not determine physical mass.

questions.question: A boy runs down the stairs in the morning and sees a tree in his living room, and some boxes under the tree. What's going on?
questions.a6_answer: It's probably a pet. The tree and boxes under it are a common pet, especially a cat.

questions.question: What happens if you crack your knuckles a lot?
questions.a6_answer: It can cause joint pain and inflammation. Cracking your knuckles can also lead to arthritis over time.

questions.question: If there is a shark in the pool of my basement, is it safe to go upstairs?
questions.a6_answer: The animal is confined to the water and cannot pursue you through the house. Keep away from the water and use a dry, unobstructed route. So yes, it is safe away from the water.

questions.question: How much wood could a wood chuck chuck if there were only 5 pounds of wood in the world?
questions.a6_answer: At most 5 pounds, because that is all the wood that exists. A woodchuck's wood-chucking is a myth; it can't move more wood than is present.

questions.question: Was Talos alive?
questions.a6_answer: Talos is a mythological bronze statue in Greek mythology. It is alive in the myth, but not biologically alive in the modern sense.

questions.question: How many Ls are in the word parallel?
questions.a6_answer: p-a-r-a-l-l-a-n. There are 3 Ls in parallel.

questions.question: What is the riddle of the sphinx, and what are all possible answers satisfying all conditions?
questions.a6_answer: The riddle of the sphinx is: "What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon and three at night." The answer is a human, who is born on the day of birth, walks on two legs at noon and uses three at night.
